picks.title: Changes in Service Use Following the Introduction of AI-Enabled Prior Authorization in Medicare
picks.take: JAMA examines what happened to service use after Medicare introduced AI-enabled prior authorization. Nothing says efficiency like teaching software to ask whether you really need that, then measuring how many people stop asking the doctor.

picks.title: Popular AI models get medication doses wrong, some dangerously: Doximity
picks.take: Doximity reports that popular AI models get medication doses wrong, some dangerously. Reassuring news for anyone worried the chatbot might take their job: it can't yet be trusted to count milligrams.

picks.title: AI vendors, health systems join physicians in liability for clinical AI
picks.take: The AMA says AI vendors and health systems now share liability with physicians. Finally, a true multidisciplinary team: everyone gets a seat at the table when the lawsuit arrives, though the doctor still signs the note.

picks.title: AI doctors' orders come with a sky-high bill
picks.take: Nature reports that AI doctors' orders come with a sky-high bill. Turns out the machine that never tires also never skips the extra test, and someone still has to pay for the full workup.

picks.title: Why every health care AI company must face Epic
picks.take: STAT investigates how Epic's market dominance shapes health tech innovation and AI adoption. Every startup has a bold vision for transforming care, right up until it needs a login to the one system everyone already uses.

picks.title: FDA, CMS scramble to avoid regulatory logjam as more states look to test AI in clinical settings
picks.take: FDA and CMS are reportedly scrambling to avoid a logjam as states move to test AI in clinical settings. Federalism, where fifty laboratories of democracy meet one regulatory agency trying to keep the experiment from becoming the standard of care.

picks.title: An AI Agent Injected Drugs Into a Live Mouse’s Brain
picks.take: Wired reports a startup let an AI agent choose a gene therapy and inject it into a live mouse's brain. The mouse never signed a consent form, but the IRB paperwork for the next step will be extraordinary.

picks.title: Putting conversational AI to the test in primary care
picks.take: Nature Medicine looks at putting conversational AI to the test in primary care. Testing before deployment is a refreshing idea in a field where the usual order is deploy, enthuse, then study.

picks.title: Health Systems Govern Only the Tip of the AI Iceberg
picks.take: NEJM AI editorial argues health systems govern only the tip of the AI iceberg. Medicine's relationship with the iceberg is well documented: committees convene, charters are drafted, and the hull is somebody else's department.

picks.title: Frights, Fangs, and Healthcare Nightmares in Winning Halloween Haikus
picks.take: KFF Health News publishes winning Halloween haikus about measles, dental costs and AI-powered insurance denials. Satire struggles when the actual healthcare system already supplies the horror, but seventeen syllables is a decent appeal length.
